general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours (60 session) + 1h final exam + 90' practical exam + 102.5h self-study. EXTRA: 6 additional evaluation sessions for group project (Session 61–66) are outside the official 150h allocation
general_information.Description: Upon completion of this course students should: 1. Understand the followings: • Data acquisition, data quality, and the end-to-end data handling pipeline • Data wrangling concepts: missing values, data types, normalization, encoding • Exploratory data analysis (EDA) and statistical reasoning (correlation, ANOVA, chi-square) • Visualization principles and data storytelling for different audiences • Dashboarding concepts and Power BI semantic modeling (star schema, relationships, measures) 2. Be able to: • Load data from CSV/Excel/JSON/SQL into Python (Pandas) and export results for reuse • Clean and transform data in Python and Excel/Power Query to prepare analytical datasets • Build effective charts with Matplotlib/Seaborn/Folium and communicate insights • Develop interactive Power BI reports/dashboards and publish to Power BI Service • Apply a simple predictive model (regression) to support data-driven decision making 3. Be able to work in team and present results with reproducible notebooks and dashboards
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: - Internet - Laptop - Python 3.x, Jupyter Notebook (Anaconda) or VS Code - Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, scikit-learn, folium - Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365) and Power BI Desktop - Optional: SQLite (sqlite3), DAX Studio (for advanced DAX debugging) - LMS/FLM for submissions and resources

description: Upon completion of this course students should: 1. Understand the followings: • Data acquisition, data quality, and the end-to-end data handling pipeline • Data wrangling concepts: missing values, data types, normalization, encoding • Exploratory data analysis (EDA) and statistical reasoning (correlation, ANOVA, chi-square) • Visualization principles and data storytelling for different audiences • Dashboarding concepts and Power BI semantic modeling (star schema, relationships, measures) 2. Be able to: • Load data from CSV/Excel/JSON/SQL into Python (Pandas) and export results for reuse • Clean and transform data in Python and Excel/Power Query to prepare analytical datasets • Build effective charts with Matplotlib/Seaborn/Folium and communicate insights • Develop interactive Power BI reports/dashboards and publish to Power BI Service • Apply a simple predictive model (regression) to support data-driven decision making 3. Be able to work in team and present results with reproducible notebooks and dashboards

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Apply data handling techniques (import, clean, transform, summarize) to prepare datasets for analysis in Python/Excel/Power Query.
Communicate insights using data storytelling: select audience-appropriate narratives, annotate visuals, and write concise interpretations.
Create clear and accurate visualizations in Python (Matplotlib/Seaborn/Folium), choosing suitable chart types and design best practices.
Build interactive dashboards in Power BI using good data modeling (relationships/star schema) and DAX measures, then publish and share responsibly.
